segments.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ מִשְּׂדֵה לָבָן שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכּוֹ, לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׂדֵה לָבָן הַסְּמוּכָה לָעִיר, אֲבָל בִּשְׂדֵה לָבָן הַסְּמוּכָה לִשְׂדֵה הָאִילָן — אֲפִילּוּ כְּדַרְכּוֹ, שֶׁמָּא יֵצְאוּ מִשְּׂדֵה הַלָּבָן וְיַחְרִיבוּ אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת.
segments.en: «It is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: When they said» that one may trap moles and mice «in a field of grain» on the intermediate days of a Festival only in a way that is «not his» usual «manner, they spoke only with regard to a field of grain» that is «adjacent to the city,» where the damage is limited to that field and is not extensive. «But in a field of grain» that is «adjacent to an orchard,» one may trap «even in his» usual «manner, lest» the moles and mice «leave the field of grain and destroy the trees» in the adjacent orchard, causing great damage.

moves.cueHe: תניא רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר כשאמרו
moves.summary: limits the rule to a grain field near the city

edges.about: the unusual-manner rule applies only to a grain field near the city, not one near an orchard

positions.claim: a grain field adjacent to an orchard may be trapped in the usual manner
